items.title: The Forensic Audit of Joseph Smith: Seer Stones, Forgeries, and Folk Magic
items.summary: Mormon News Roundup's episode examines the physical evidence surrounding Joseph Smith's claims, including the seer stone and hat, the Toronto copyright revelation, and the rewriting of the 1833 Book of Commandments.

items.title: Proposed data center on land leased from LDS Church moves forward
items.summary: The Salt Lake Tribune reports that Cottle County, Texas, commissioners unanimously endorsed a special reinvestment zone covering 4,252 acres, much of it held by the church's Farmland Reserve subsidiary, and approved a tax abatement request from developer Aetheris for a proposed 96-megawatt data center. An AgReserve statement cited by the Tribune says Aetheris is independent and "not affiliated with Farmland Reserve or the church."

items.title: Former BYU standout Parker Kingston’s lawyers say prosecutor has a conflict of interest, ask judge to remove him from rape case
items.summary: The Salt Lake Tribune reports that lawyers for former BYU football standout Parker Kingston want the prosecutor removed from his rape case, arguing that a disciplinary complaint the prosecutor filed against lawyers who criticized the investigation on TikTok creates a conflict of interest.

items.title: LDS Apostle Under the Microscope!
items.summary: Mormon Discussions says RFM and Bill Reel do a deep dive into the recent worldwide devotional given by Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles.

items.title: 19-year-old LDS missionary dies in the Philippines
items.summary: The Salt Lake Tribune reports that a 19-year-old missionary died while serving in his Philippines homeland, and that at least three other missionaries have died in the past three months.
